sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Virginia Tech researchers used Sentinel-1 satellite radar data to track land movement in 20 African coastal cities. They found cities including Lagos, Alexandria and Luanda are sinking faster than estimated by the IPCC in 2021. Alexandria and Lagos are sinking by an average of 6mm and 5mm per year respectively, while Durban has remained stable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Subsidence lowers land relative to the sea, compounding climate-driven sea level rises. Alexandria faces sea level rises 36% higher by 2050 than previously projected. Seven million people and $180bn of assets could be at flood risk. Groundwater extraction, land reclamation and sediment trapping by the Aswan Dam contribute to the sinking.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Researchers suggest the satellite monitoring technique could be applied to regions like the Pacific islands. Better data may help African planners allocate resources, establish local policies to manage water extraction, supply alternative water sources, and construct flood defences.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Model and artist Veruschka, born Vera von Lehndorff, has died at the age of 87. Born in 1939, she endured a traumatic childhood after her father was executed in 1944 for plotting to assassinate Adolf Hitler. She subsequently rose to fame in the 1960s as one of fashion's original supermodels.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Veruschka expanded the boundaries of fashion and beauty through body-transforming art and major collaborations with designers and photographers. A former Metropolitan Police officer provided misleading evidence leading to Kololo's conviction.
Kololo's conviction was quashed, and he is now suing the Met for compensation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In 2011, Somali gunmen killed David Tebbutt and abducted his wife Judith in Kenya. Kenyan police arrested Ali Kololo, a woodcutter, and tortured him into signing a statement. Metropolitan Police officers assisted the investigation. Former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd presented misleading evidence and relied on Kololo's coerced statement, leading to Kololo's wrongful conviction for kidnap and robbery.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Kololo spent over ten years in prison, including three years on death row, before Kenya's High Court quashed his conviction in 2023. The Independent Office for Police Conduct found Hibberd had omitted forensic evidence. The wrongful imprisonment destroyed Kololo's health, marriage and family life, leaving him unable to work or support his children.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kololo is suing London's Metropolitan Police for compensation to rebuild his life and support his children. The Metropolitan Police force is contesting the legal claim, which lawyers say could take years to resolve.
